name: cut-through-reference
description: A zero-buffer cut-through 100 Mbps Ethernet switch ASIC (Essenceia/ethernet_switch_asic, commit a14e3e1), as its RTL behaves in simulation; not measured silicon. See doc/latency-model.md.
notes: One RMII clock of 50 MHz (20 ns, 2 bits per cycle) for all ports. First preamble bit in to first preamble bit out: 63 cycles (1260 ns), whatever the frame length. The decision needs the 8 bytes of preamble and delimiter and the 6-byte destination MAC (14 bytes).

A frame is forwarded on a port only if it would start there at least 51 cycles (1020 ns) after the first idle cycle that followed the previous frame; otherwise it is dropped on that port. One lookup per cycle; within a cycle the lowest port index wins and the others are dropped on all ports.

Address table: 4 entries, learned on every frame from its source MAC (not group addresses), the oldest replaced when full, a lifetime of 300 s (the author's write-up); the age counter's 4-bit steps are not modelled.
No FCS check: corrupted frames are forwarded.
